title: PostgreSQL Read-Replica Replication Lag Spike
error_signature: psycopg2.OperationalError: replication lag exceeds threshold (942 seconds)

File '/app/db/replica_monitor.py', line 58, in check_health
  raise ReplicationLagAlert(f'Replica lag {lag_seconds}s > 300s threshold')
root_cause: A large unindexed batch analytics query ran directly against the read-replica, locking the replication stream buffer.
runbook_steps: Identify blocking query PID using: SELECT pid, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state != 'idle';
Terminate query: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(blocking_pid);
Route analytics queries strictly to the dedicated reporting warehouse, not operational read-replicas.
anti_patterns: DO NOT rebuild the replica from scratch; replica catching up takes 4 hours and degrades read traffic.
deployment_context: Analytics cron job deployed 2 days prior.

title: GitHub: Github Mlag Stonith Splitbrain
error_signature: CRITICAL_ALERT: GitHub service degradation (network_fault) - Github Mlag Stonith Splitbrain

**Timeline:**
1. **20:15:00** — Aggregation switch agent on agg-switch-a terminated for maintenance state dump; links stayed UP.
2. **20:15:05** — agg-switch-b lost heartbeat to peer (agent down) but detected peer links were still UP, triggering DISRUPTIVE (not gentle) MLAG failover.
3. **20:15:06–20:16:36** — Spanning-tree reconvergence blocked ALL inter-rack L2 traffic for ~90 seconds.
4. **20:16:40** — Pacemaker heartbeat between fileserver pairs timed out (heartbeat runs on the same production fabric now blacked out), each pair declared the other dead.
5. **20:16:43** — When network recovered, **both members of each pair simultaneously believed they were active** and issued mutual STONITH fencing → **both shut down**.
6. **Result** — All 4 DRBD resources now have NO Primary; automatic recovery is unsafe (booting the stale node first risks data overwrite).
root_cause: Pacemaker cluster heartbeat (running on production L2 fabric) timed out during a 90-second inter-rack spanning-tree reconvergence triggered by MLAG disruptive failover; when the network recovered, both members of each pair issued simultaneous mutual STONITH fences, stopping all 4 fileservers and leaving all DRBD resources with no Primary.
runbook_steps: Boot fileserver-pair1-a-0 (the last confirmed Primary per DRBD generation logs in the startup message) and allow it to become Primary; once healthy, boot the passive peers in order (pair1-b-0, pair2-a-0, pair2-b-0) to allow DRBD re-sync and restore the active pair count to 4.
